questions.text: The ratio of electric force to gravitational force between two particles having charges $q_1, q_2$ and masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ respectively is (where symbols have their usual meanings)
questions.solution: $F_g = \frac{G m_1 m_2}{r^2}$, $F_e = \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2} \Rightarrow \frac{F_e}{F_g} = \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 G m_1 m_2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Match the column appropriately regarding thermodynamic process.

Column-I:
(P) When volume change is zero
(Q) When pressure is constant
(R) When no heat is exchanged
(S) Work done by the gas is equal to heat given to the gas

Column-II:
(i) $\Delta W = 0$
(ii) $\Delta Q = 0$
(iii) Isobaric
(iv) Isothermal
questions.solution:
Volume change is zero $\rightarrow$ Isochoric $\rightarrow \Delta W = 0$
Isobaric $\Rightarrow \Delta P = 0$
No heat exchange (adiabatic) $\Rightarrow \Delta Q = 0$
Heat given = $\Delta W \Rightarrow \Delta U = 0 \Rightarrow \Delta T = 0$ (Isothermal)

questions.solution: $i = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{12}{12} = 1\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Statement-I : Hot water is less viscous than of cold water.
Statement-II : Surface tension of soap bubble is more than that of a drop of water.
options: Statement-I is true and statement-II true
Statement-I is true and statement-II false
Statement-I is false and statement-II true

options: Current in the circuit is zero
Voltage across the capacitor is minimum
Current in the circuit is maximum
questions.solution: Immediately after closing the key, the capacitor acts as a short circuit (path of zero resistance). Hence, current is maximum at $t = 0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A uniform solid sphere of mass $m$ rolls down from rest to achieve speed $v_1$ on an inclined plane of $30^\circ$. Sphere achieves speed $v_2$ on an inclined plane of $45^\circ$ when released from same height then $\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2}$ is (assume no slipping)
questions.solution: $|\Delta U| = |\Delta K| \Rightarrow mgh = \frac{1}{2}(\gamma + 1)mv^2$ where $\gamma = \frac{2}{5}$. Here $v$ doesn't depend on $\theta$, so $\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2} = 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Find the equation of magnetic field for the give equation of electric field (for EM wave).
$\vec{E} = E_0 (4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j})\cos(\omega t - kz)$
questions.solution: Phase difference of magnetic field with electric field is zero. Also $|\vec{B}| = \frac{E_0 \cdot 5}{C}$. Propagation direction is along $\vec{E} \times \vec{B} = \hat{k}$, so unit vector along $\vec{B}$ is $\frac{3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}}{5}$. Hence $\vec{B} = \frac{E_0}{C}(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\cos(\omega t - kz)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two objects are equal distances from sphere of radius $R$ & refractive index $\mu$ such that the image of one object forms on other object. Find the object distance from the surface of sphere.
questions.solution:
After first refraction the ray must become parallel to the line joining two objects, so $v = \infty$.
$\frac{\mu_2}{v} - \frac{\mu_1}{u} = \frac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R} \Rightarrow 0 - \frac{1}{-u} = \frac{\mu - 1}{R} \Rightarrow |u| = \frac{R}{\mu - 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a radioactive decay, decay constant of element $A_2$ is 3 times that of element $A_1$. Find the ratio of nuclei of element 1 to element 2 after one half life of $A_2$ (Assume initial number of nuclei are same for both elements)
questions.solution:
$N_1 = N_0 e^{-\lambda_1 t}$, $N_2 = N_0 e^{-\lambda_2 t}$
$\frac{N_1}{N_2} = e^{(\lambda_2 - \lambda_1)t} = e^{(3\lambda_1 - \lambda_1)\frac{\ln 2}{3\lambda_1}} = e^{\frac{2}{3} \ln 2} = 2^{2/3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A bullet of kinetic energy of $125\text{ J}$ strikes a lead block where temperature rises by $50^\circ\text{C}$. If specific heat of lead is $0.1\text{ J/g-}^\circ\text{C}$ then mass of lead block is (Assume half of kinetic energy of bullet is converted to heat) $m\text{ gram}$ then $2m$ is
questions.solution: $Q = ms\Delta T \Rightarrow \frac{125}{2} = m \times 0.1 \times 50 \Rightarrow m = 12.5\text{ gm} \Rightarrow 2m = 25$

questions.text: Co2+ is forming an octahedral complex with spin only magnetic moment 3.83 BM. The correct electronic configuration for cobalt in the complex is?
questions.solution: Since Co2+ has magnetic moment 3.83 BM, it has 3 unpaired electrons (3d7 weak field ligand). So electronic configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry

Consider the following Latimer diagram
$\text{FeO}_4^{2-} \xrightarrow{2.0\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^{3+} \xrightarrow{0.8\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^{2+} \xrightarrow{-0.5\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^0$
Find $E^\circ_{\text{FeO}_4^{2-}/\text{Fe}^{2+}}$.
questions.solution: $-4 \times F \times E^\circ = -3 \times F \times 2 + (-1 \times F \times 0.8) \Rightarrow -4E = -6.8 \Rightarrow E = 1.7\text{ V} \approx 2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the given values :
$\Delta H = 55\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta S = 175\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$
$T = 25^\circ\text{C}$
Calculate the value of Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G$) in $\text{J mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = 55000 - 298 \times 175 = 2850\text{ J mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The sum of all rational terms in the expansion of $\left(1 + 2^{1/3} + 3^{1/2}\right)^6$ is
questions.solution:
General term: $\frac{6!}{\alpha! \beta! \gamma!} 1^\alpha (2^{1/3})^\beta (3^{1/2})^\gamma$. For rational terms $3|\beta$ and $2|\gamma$.
Sum of rational terms = $27 + 45 + 135 + 27 + 40 + 360 + 4 = 638$.

questions.solution:
$\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(\frac{2e^{2x}}{1+e^{2x}}\right)y = \frac{6}{1+e^{2x}}$. IF = $1 + e^{2x}$.
$y(1+e^{2x}) = 6x + C$. Passes through $(0, 0) \Rightarrow C = 0$.
At $x = \ln 2$, $k(1+4) = 6 \ln 2 \Rightarrow k = \frac{6}{5}\ln 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$, where
$f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{2}{x}(\sin(k_1 + 1)x + \sin(k_2 + 1)x) & x < 0 \\ 4 & x = 0 \\ \frac{2}{x}\log\left[\frac{k_2 x + 1}{k_1 x + 1}\right] & x > 0 \end{cases}$
Then $k_1^2 + k_2^2$ is
questions.solution:
LHL = $2(k_1 + 1 + k_2 + 1) = 4 \Rightarrow k_1 + k_2 = 0$.
RHL = $2(k_2 - k_1) = 4 \Rightarrow k_2 - k_1 = 2$.
Solving gives $k_1 = -1, k_2 = 1 \Rightarrow k_1^2 + k_2^2 = 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the equation $a(b - c)x^2 + b(c - a)x + c(a - b) = 0$ has equal roots and if $a + c = 5$ and $b = \frac{16}{5}$, then the value of $a^2 + c^2$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Root is 1, so other root is also 1 $\Rightarrow \frac{c(a-b)}{a(b-c)} = 1 \Rightarrow 2ac = b(a+c) = \frac{16}{5}(5) = 16$.
$a^2 + c^2 = (a+c)^2 - 2ac = 25 - 16 = 9$.

questions.solution: Intersection points: $(-3, 4)$ and $(4, 3)$. Area = $\frac{1}{4}(75\pi + 2) \Rightarrow \alpha = 75, \beta = 2 \Rightarrow \alpha + \beta = 77$.
